Such regime/continuity uncertainty typically triggers a risk-off reflex: equities sell, volatility rises. However the sign is genuinely ambiguous because some market participants view a change in leadership (and associated tariff/trade-policy posture) as neutral-to-positive, which caps both the magnitude and the confidence of a directional call.

predictions.reasoning: Gold is the cleaner safe-haven proxy for sudden US political/continuity shocks. A credible spike in Trump-removal odds — especially if driven by instability or a health event — would plausibly bid safe havens as investors hedge policy and governance uncertainty. The exposure is indirect and the base rate of such events is very low, so magnitude and confidence are modest.

llm_justification.summary: The market prices the probability Trump permanently leaves office before 2027. A sharp upward spike would most plausibly reflect a sudden continuity shock (health, resignation, acute crisis), implying a risk-off reflex: modest downside in US equities (SPY) and modest upside in safe havens (gold/GLD). But the sign is ambiguous, the proxies are weakly exposed, and most probability drift is noise — so confidence and magnitudes are low and below the 700bps tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: A material anomaly in this market reflects a real, near-term continuity event rather than idle speculation
Such an event would register as broad political-risk uncertainty for US assets
Safe havens respond more cleanly than equities, whose direction depends on the cause
failure_modes: The probability move is pure noise with no underlying event, so no asset reaction occurs
The event is already public by the time it hits prediction markets, leaving no tradable edge
Equities rally instead of fall if markets view leadership change as policy-friendly, inverting the thesis
Gold fails to respond if the dollar simultaneously spikes on the same risk event
Low base rate means false positives dominate; the signal is more likely wrong than right
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
